newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles mayor proposes $4 bln budget - paper.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles mayor proposes $4 bln budget - paper.

text.p: Los Angeles Mayor Richard Riordan unveiled his $4 billion budget plan for fiscal year 1997-98 and promised to support a $465 million bond issue to fund city police and fire facilities, according to a newspaper report on Saturday.
The new spending plan -- $50 million smaller than last year's budget -- would cut 470 jobs and seek no new taxes, the Los Angeles Times reported.

The budget, presented by the mayor on Friday, would rely less on one-time funds to cut the city's structural deficit, the Times reported. With these changes, Riordan's office has forecast a small surplus in five years.

The mayor also announced plans to support two large ballot measures. One bond issue would provide up to $465 million for police and fire facilities. The other would raise about $150 million for library improvements, the Times reported.
The full city council is expected to begin debating the mayor's budget plan on May 19.
